name: Circle of Willis and Neurovascular Stroke Syndromes

reference.source: Clinical Neuroanatomy Made Ridiculously Simple / Brazis Localization
clinicalPearls: Circle of Willis polygon anastomoses internal carotid and vertebrobasilar circulations at the brain base
Middle cerebral artery stroke causes contralateral hemiparesis and sensory loss predominantly affecting face and arm
Left dominant MCA stroke causes aphasia; right non-dominant MCA stroke produces hemineglect and anosognosia
Anterior cerebral artery stroke impairs contralateral leg and foot function with urinary incontinence
Saccular berry aneurysms occur most commonly at anterior communicating artery bifurcation (35%)
reference.pathophysiology: The Circle of Willis provides collateral perfusion across cerebral hemispheres. Thromboembolic or atherothrombotic occlusion of specific branches causes territorial ischemic stroke corresponding to somatotopic cortical representations. Saccular aneurysms arise at arterial branch points from internal elastic lamina defects and rupture into the subarachnoid space.
additionalInvestigations: Non-contrast head CT to exclude acute hemorrhage
Diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) brain for early cytotoxic edema
CT or MR angiography from aortic arch to vertex to identify vessel occlusion or aneurysm
